observador.title: 22h. UE escolhe dois portugueses como embaixadores
observador.description: Kaja Kallas anunciou hoje a escolha de 33 embaixadores noutros países. Ainda assim, o Presidente da República destaca o contributo dos imigrantes para o funcionamento das misericórdias.

observador.title: Homem de 68 anos morre em despiste de mota no IP4
observador.description: Um homem morreu na sequência de um despiste de motociclo no IP4, próximo de Vila Real, avançou a GNR.

observador.title: Fiat mostra Grizzly e Grizzly Fastback para combater Duster
observador.description: A Fiat revelou com que "armas" pretende disputar o mercado com modelos como o Dacia Duster. O novo Grizzly vai permitir à marca bater-se com os SUV do segmento C, com mais espaço no habitáculo e mala.

observador.title: Declarações de Rubio "difamam" China, diz Pequim
observador.description: A China acusa o secretário de Estado norte-americano de difamação, depois de este ter homenageado as vítimas da repressão na Praça Tiananmen, condenando "a censura" do regime chinês.

observador.title: 21h. Zelensky pede reunião a Putin para o fim da guerra
observador.description: O Presidente ucraniano propôs um encontro com Putin com o objetivo de pôr fim à guerra. Ainda assim, o Tribunal da Relação ordenou repetir o julgamento da ex-deputada do PAN Cristina Rodrigues.

observador.title: 20h. Isabel dos Santos agiu de boa fé, conclui Tribunal
observador.description: A Relação de Lisboa diz que "não existe qualquer conclusão judicial de que a aquisição da EFACEC tenha sido financiada pelo Estado angolano. Ainda , Mariana Leitão acusa o Chega de não ser sério.

observador.title: Espólio de Prince lança álbum com raridades
observador.description: Uma nova coleção póstuma de Prince, Timeless, será lançada em 28 de agosto, mas o primeiro single, "Stone", uma gravação de 1995, já foi divulgado.

observador.title: Seguro alerta que envelhecimento é "bomba-relógio"
observador.description: O Presidente da República alerta que o envelhecimento do país constitui uma "bomba-relógio". Seguro defende que Estado deve dar uma resposta melhor.

observador.title: Relação manda repetir julgamento de Cristina Rodrigues
observador.description: Tribunal da Relação anulou decisão do tribunal de primeira instância que absolveu Cristina Rodrigues, acusada de "apagão informático" de emails do partido, e mandou repetir julgamento.

observador.title: Setor da IA pede que Congresso proteja EUA de ameaças
observador.description: Executivos da indústria da inteligência artificial e um grupo de especialistas em segurança nacional pediram ao Congresso dos EUA que proteja o país das ameaças biológicas, potenciadas pela tecnologia

observador.title: Eugen Tomac nomeado primeiro-ministro da Roménia
observador.description: O Presidente romeno nomeou o eurodeputado Eugen Tomac como primeiro-ministro, um mês após a destituição do liberal Ilie Bolojan. Vai propor "um governo técnico e não político".

observador.title: Sebastião Bugalho: "Aqui ninguém me liga nenhuma"
observador.description: O Observador entrevistou Sebastião Bugalho em Estrasburgo numa entrevista com regras: evitar assuntos de atualidade, ser realizada num bar e acompanhada de uma cerveja.

observador.title: Richard Gere apela a que se abordem migrações de forma moral
observador.description: Richard Gere apelou a que se abordem as causas profundas da migração e que se encare este fenómeno numa perspetiva moral e não apenas com políticas restritivas e de segurança.

observador.title: 19h. Spinumviva. Montenegro recorreu ao TC sobre declarações
observador.description: Montenegro recusa ter apresentado “novos recursos” contra as decisões da Entidade para a Transparência. Ainda, Isabel dos Santos festeja a decisão do Tribunal da Relação de Lisboa sobre Efacec.

observador.title: Injeções para emagrecer podem baixar risco de cancro da mama
observador.description: Três estudos apresentados nos Estados Unidos associam a utilização de medicamentos para emagrecer com a hormona GLP-1 com a redução dos riscos de desenvolver cancro ou morrer da doença.

observador.title: As primeiras horas dos duques de Edimburgo em Portugal
observador.description: Seguimos atrás de Eduardo e Sophie, que passaram por Lisboa esta semana, entre datas históricas e referências bem típicas da capital portuguesa.

spiegel.title: »Schöne, saubere Kohle« – Trump kündigt 700 Millionen Dollar für fossile Energie an
spiegel.description: Neue Kohlekraftwerke, der Ausbau von Bergbau und ein neuer Hafen: US-Präsident Donald Trump will Millionen in die Energiegewinnung aus Kohle stecken. Klimaschutz hält er für »Betrug«.

spiegel.title: Andoni Iraola wird neuer Trainer beim FC Liverpool
spiegel.description: Nach einer erfolgreichen Zeit bei Bournemouth wartet auf den Spanier Andoni Iraola die größte Trainerstation seiner Karriere: Ab Juli übernimmt er den FC Liverpool, der eine verkorkste Saison hinter sich hat.

spiegel.title: Richard Gere: Umgang mit Geflüchteten – US-Schauspieler schämt sich für sein Land
spiegel.description: Der US-Schauspieler Richard Gere (»Pretty Woman«) ist ein scharfer Trump-Kritiker. Bei einer Veranstaltung in Berlin ging er mit der US-Migrationspolitik hart ins Gericht.

spiegel.title: »Maskenmann«: Martin Ney in Nantes zu lebenslanger Haft wegen Mordes an Jonathan C. verurteilt
spiegel.description: Jahrelang hat er Kinder sexuell missbraucht, mehrere Jungen ermordete er. Nun wurde der »Maskenmann« für den Mord an dem zehnjährigen Jonathan C. in Nantes verurteilt.

spiegel.title: Ukrainekrieg: Putin und Selenskyj äußern sich zu möglichen Verhandlungen
spiegel.description: Russlands Präsident Putin sagt, er sei zu einem Deal bereit – doch konkret wird er nicht. Der ukrainische Präsident Selenskyj ruft Putin zu einem direkten Treffen auf, um über Frieden zu verhandeln.

spiegel.title: 1860 München: Investor Hasan Ismaik will Club nicht vor einer Insolvenz retten
spiegel.description: Wie geht es weiter mit 1860 München? Der Fußballclub steht nach dem Lizenzentzug vor einer ungewissen Zukunft. Investor Ismaik will eine drohende Pleite nicht verhindern. Der Stammverein hat aber ohnehin andere Pläne.

spiegel.title: Wal-Obduktion in Dänemark: Ein leises Zischen, dann entweicht die Luft aus dem Kadaver
spiegel.description: »Guck mal Papa, das Blut«: Auf der dänischen Insel Anholt wird der Buckelwal obduziert, der Deutschland monatelang beschäftigte. Was sagen die Forscher, die das Tier zerlegen?

spiegel.title: Fleurance – Frankreich: Polizisten finden Kinderleiche auf Suche nach Elfjähriger
spiegel.description: Seit Tagen wird ein Mädchen in Frankreich vermisst. Doch Suchtrupps kamen offenbar zu spät. Ein Tatverdächtiger ist festgenommen worden. Dass er überhaupt noch frei herumlief, beschäftigt jetzt die Politik.

spiegel.title: Obduktion von Buckelwal »Timmy« in Dänemark: SPIEGEL-Reporter berichtet von Insel Anholt
spiegel.description: Spielende Kinder, Omas auf Sitzkissen, Männer mit Bier: Die Obduktion des gestrandeten Buckelwals ist für die Dänen nichts Besonderes. Sie wundert das große Interesse der Deutschen, sagt SPIEGEL-Reporter Jonathan Stock.

spiegel.title: Dokumentenaffäre: Trumps Ex-Berater Bolton will sich laut Medienberichten schuldig bekennen
spiegel.description: Hat der ehemalige Sicherheitsberater von Donald Trump illegal Geheimdokumente aufbewahrt? Laut US-Medienberichten will John Bolton diese Straftat vor Gericht einräumen. Bisher hatte er auf nicht schuldig plädiert.

spiegel.title: Lufthansa – Flughafen Frankfurt: Mehrere Menschen nach Vorfall im Krankenhaus
spiegel.description: An einem Gate des Frankfurter Flughafens gab plötzlich das Bugfahrwerk einer Lufthansa-Maschine nach. Mitglieder der Crew und des Bodenpersonals wurden verletzt. Die Bilder erinnern an einen Fall aus London im Jahr 2021.

spiegel.title: Buckelwal vor Anholt: Erste Obduktionsergebnisse – »Timmy« war ein Mädchen
spiegel.description: Noch läuft die Untersuchung des Walkadavers auf der dänischen Insel Anholt, doch erste Ergebnisse gibt es bereits. So wurde der Gebärmutterhals des Tieres freigelegt. Die Todesursache des Tieres ist weiterhin unklar.

spiegel.title: Manfred Hamm: Mit seiner Kamera fing er die Magie ein - Nachruf
spiegel.description: Seine Bilder von verlassenen Industriebauten waren genrebildend, die von der Berliner Mauer gehören zu den schönsten Zeitdokumenten dieses traurigen Baus. Erinnerung an den Fotografen Manfred Hamm.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Es ist nicht irgendein Fritze, es ist der Bundeskanzler
spiegel.description: Ehrfurcht vor politischen Ämtern haben wir aus guten Gründen verloren. Den Respekt aber sollten wir behalten. Schon aus eigenem Interesse.

spiegel.title: Kroatien: Vier Tote bei Absturz von Kleinflugzeug
spiegel.description: Ein in Deutschland registriertes Kleinflugzeug ist über der kroatischen Halbinsel Istrien verunglückt. Es gibt keine überlebenden Insassen. Die Unfallursache wird noch ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Pflegereform: Nina Warken spart bei den Falschen - Kommentar
spiegel.description: Pflegende Angehörige entlasten den Staat um Milliarden. Doch ihre Rentenansprüche wird die Pflegeversicherung künftig nicht mehr zahlen. Damit steigt das Armutsrisiko, vor allem für Frauen.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Gericht verurteilt Mann nach Schüssen in Hamburg zu langer Haftstrafe
spiegel.description: Wegen eines Kiosks und unbezahlter Steuern eskalierte ein Streit in Hamburg-Billstedt. Ein Mensch starb. Das Landgericht hat den Schützen zu zehneinhalb Jahren Gefängnis verurteilt.

spiegel.title: Insel Ostervilm: So lief die Versteigerung der ehemaligen DDR-Militärstation vor Rügen
spiegel.description: Die Versteigerung einer Insel vor Rügen erregte bundesweite Aufmerksamkeit. Den Zuschlag bekam ein Mann, der die heruntergekommene Militärstation darauf noch nie gesehen hat. Was er mit dem künstlichen Eiland vorhat.

elpais.title: La directora de la Guardia Civil dice que cortó con Leire Díez cuando esta le pidió que recuperara a un comandante implicado en el ‘caso Koldo’
elpais.description: Mercedes González asegura que mantuvo dos citas con Díez en las que no habló de las investigaciones contra el PSOE y que interrumpió la relación cuando la espía planteó su teoría de la conspiración

elpais.description: La oposición ha debatido este jueves en la Asamblea de Madrid sobre la falta de climatización de las aulas de los colegios madrileños, a lo que Mariano de Paco ha respondido que “cuando hace calor, hace calor”

elpais.title: España se va a América tras una pachanga ante Irak
elpais.description: La selección, plagada de debutantes y meritorios que no irán al Mundial, firma un tibio empate

elpais.description: Los actos y los desplazamientos en papamóvil de León XIV entre el 6 y el 12 de junio provocará cortes de calles, desvíos y alteraciones en el transporte público

elpais.title: Sánchez acompañará al papa León XIV en su encuentro con migrantes en el muelle de Arguineguín
elpais.description: Supervivientes de la ruta atlántica relatarán su experiencia durante la que será la primera visita de un pontífice a Canarias

elpais.title: Estados Unidos sanciona al presidente de Cuba y al entorno familiar de Raúl Castro
elpais.description: El Departamento del Tesoro anuncia medidas financieras contra los parientes políticos de Miguel Díaz-Canel y contra las Fuerzas Armadas

elpais.title: Ignacio Dancausa, el joven apadrinado de Ayuso, se hace con la presidencia de Nuevas Generaciones del PP
elpais.description: Los dos candidatos que habían logrado los avales necesarios han acordado una lista de unidad para el congreso de julio

elpais.title: El exasesor de Trump John Bolton se declarará culpable de manejo indebido de documentos clasificados
elpais.description: El antiguo consejero de Seguridad Nacional se enfrenta a 18 cargos de tenencia indebida y transmisión de información que afectaba a la defensa nacional

elpais.description: El foro económico palidece tras cuatro años de guerra, pero se siguen tejiendo lealtades y contratos entre bambalinas

elpais.description: El atasco en las conversaciones en Oriente Próximo agota la paciencia del Capitolio y provoca la revuelta de quienes no buscan la reelección en noviembre y por eso no temen la ira del presidente

elpais.title: Petro cede y descarta la idea de convocar una Constituyente
elpais.description: El comité que promovía la reforma a la Constitución de 1991, un proyecto que había despertado críticas y temores, da a conocer la decisión, que reformula el panorama electoral a dos semanas de la segunda vuelta

elpais.title: Muere la historietista y cineasta Marjane Satrapi, autora de ‘Persépolis’, a los 56 años
elpais.description: La familia de la dibujante francoiraní de cómics informa de que ha fallecido “de tristeza” tras la muerte de su marido hace un año

elpais.title: El 65% de profesores catalanes votan no al pacto educativo y anuncian nuevas huelgas la próxima semana
elpais.description: Educación anuncia que aplicará el nuevo acuerdo, después de que Profesores de Secundaria anuncie que lo firmará

nyt.title: John Bolton, Ex-Trump Adviser, Reaches Deal to Plead Guilty Over Classified Information
nyt.description: The former Trump national security adviser plans to plead guilty to a count of illegal retention of classified information, which could result in a fine and possibly prison time of up to five years.

nyt.title: Several Women Who Dated Graham Platner Recall ‘Unsettling’ Behavior
nyt.description: The Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine could be charming, women said in interviews, but some found his actions intimidating and disturbing.

nyt.title: Early Research Suggests a Path to Predict and Prevent Lung Cancer
nyt.description: Scientists have identified proteins that could signal increased lung cancer risk, as well as a drug that could reduce the odds of a tumor developing.

nyt.title: Wall Street Is Going Gaga for SpaceX
nyt.description: Jamie Dimon himself is planning to pitch investors on the offering of Elon Musk’s rocket company, as banks prepare to reap huge fees from the largest I.P.O. ever.

nyt.title: Gwynne Shotwell, Elon Musk’s No. 2 at SpaceX, Is the Company’s Steady Hand
nyt.description: Gwynne Shotwell, the president and chief operating officer, is the adult-in-the-room foil to Mr. Musk as SpaceX prepares for a blockbuster initial public offering.

nyt.title: Netflix’s New Movie Strategy: Fewer, Better Films
nyt.description: Dan Lin doesn’t fawn over stars or write blank checks. And he still greenlights more movies than anyone.

nyt.title: Ultra-Orthodox Riot Shocks Israelis In Latest Protest At Military Draft
nyt.description: Israel’s Haredim have escalated their protests against military service in recent weeks, underscoring growing divisions ahead of national elections.

nyt.title: Trump and Mamdani Plan to Be at Monday’s Knicks Game (but Not Together)
nyt.description: President Trump is expected to sit in a luxury box for Game 3 of the N.B.A. finals at Madison Square Garden. Mayor Zohran Mamdani says he will be in a “very different section.”

nyt.title: Why Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass Has to Fight for Her Job
nyt.description: Ms. Bass, a Democrat, has had a roller-coaster first term. She now faces the first runoff since 2005 for an incumbent mayor in the city.

nyt.title: As Trump Toughens Rules on Cuba’s Economy, Hotel Chains Withdraw
nyt.description: The Trump administration’s efforts to tighten the economic noose on Cuba appear to be working, as more international firms announced they would leave the island.

nyt.title: Amid Kennedy Center Strife, the National Symphony Faces a Cloudy Future
nyt.description: After months of uncertainty, and without an approved budget or secured venue, the orchestra has been unable to schedule its next season.

nyt.title: Kennedy Center Tells Staff to Immediately Remove Trump’s Name From Documents
nyt.description: The center’s general counsel also said that a federal judge’s order meant the president’s name must be taken off outdoor and indoor signage by June 12.

nyt.title: How LinkedIn Found Its Social Platform Era
nyt.description: Celebrities and paid influencers have transformed the career-focused platform, which for some users, has become a job unto itself.

nyt.title: 5 Minutes That Will Make You Love Charlie Parker
nyt.description: Bird helped usher in bebop and transformed the alto saxophone into an instrument of startling possibility. Here’s an 11-song primer on his enduring legacy.

nyt.title: Melinda French Gates: Women, We Deserve Better Than This
nyt.description: Too many women walk out of their doctors’ office with no diagnosis, no treatment and no plan.

nyt.title: America Doesn’t Have to Hold Unfair, Unrepresentative Elections
nyt.description: Americans should think big about shaking up how we vote.

nyt.title: What to Know About the Arrest of ICE Protesters at Delaney Hall in New Jersey
nyt.description: More than 80 people have been arrested during turbulent protests outside the Delaney Hall immigrant detention center in New Jersey over the past two weeks.

npr.title: Thousands of Albanians protest a planned luxury resort linked to Jared Kushner
npr.description: Albania braces for bigger protests as Jared Kushner-backed luxury resort sparks environmental outrage.

npr.title: North Korea unveils a new plant to produce fuel for nuclear weapons
npr.description: State media photos on the place showed it is likely a plant to produce weapons-grade uranium.

npr.title: Hezbollah rejects ceasefire deal agreed on by Israel and Lebanon
npr.description: The U.N. peacekeeping mission for Lebanon, known as UNIFIL, said one peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

npr.title: Russia's economic forum opens against backdrop of Ukrainian strikes
npr.description: The St. Petersburg International Economic Forum -- Russia's answer to Davos -- opens under the shadow of Ukrainian drone attacks and growing economic uncertainty.

npr.title: Peru election could add to string of right-wing victories in Latin America
npr.description: Peruvians go to the polls Sunday to elect their next president amid a conservative shift in Latin America. The daughter of a former dictator, a far-right senator, could win.

npr.title: Plans for a Trump family-linked resort spark protests in Albania
npr.description: A coastal development project linked to Jared Kushner is facing resistance in Albania. The government says the project will transform the nation, but environmental campaigners and critics oppose it.

npr.title: Video of a dying teen handcuffed by police sparks outrage and riots across Britain
npr.description: There is outrage in the U.K. over the murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak. Bodycam footage shows police handcuffing him as he lay dying. His killer falsely accused Nowak of racist abuse.

npr.title: Trump confirms calling Netanyahu 'crazy,' says they still get along
npr.description: The president also acknowledged that he cursed at the Israeli leader in a heated phone call in which he told Benjamin Netanyahu not to bomb the Lebanese capital Beirut.

npr.title: Greetings from Porto, whose lanes are lined with colorful textiles
npr.description: Linen scarves, cotton aprons and dishtowels adorn the entrances to souvenir shops, many of which are run by Bangladeshis whose home country shares Portugal's rich tradition of textile manufacturing.

npr.title: Ukrainian drones strike a St. Petersburg oil terminal ahead of Putin visit
npr.description: Ukrainian drones struck an oil terminal in St. Petersburg and set it ablaze, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, as the city hosted an annual economic forum promoted by President Putin.

lanacion.description: El siniestro se produjo a horas de la mañana en un centro de almacenamiento de la localidad de Tepeaca, a unos 165 kilómetros de la capital mexicana

lanacion.title: La carne vacuna registró el segundo mes consecutivo con un precio estable: aumentaron el pollo y el cerdo

lanacion.description: El minuto a minuto de las decisiones del Presidente, las reacciones de la oposición y las declaraciones de los funcionarios

lanacion.description: El doctor en Ciencias Biológicas e investigador del Conicet explica sus líneas de trabajo, que incluyen terapia regenerativa en base a implantación de neuronas y mecanismos de neuroprotección de las células que siguen vivas

lanacion.title: Lilia Lemoine criticó a Villarruel en la interna con Bullrich por los pliegos judiciales: “Cara de piedra”
lanacion.description: La legisladora se hizo eco de las críticas expresadas por la vicepresidenta ante el caos de la sesión del Senado

lanacion.description: Ruidos, objetos acumulados, luz, circulación y rutinas domésticas influyen en el humor, los vínculos y la energía diaria; por qué ciertos espacios calman, otros irritan y los pequeños ajustes que pueden producir cambios concretos

lanacion.description: Dos condiciones digestivas que ganaron protagonismo en los últimos años: qué las causa, cómo se detectan y qué dice la ciencia sobre su tratamiento

lanacion.description: Tienen beneficios para la piel y aportan nutrientes esenciales para la salud de la tiroides y los músculos

lanacion.title: El Gobierno de la Ciudad propone cambiar el nombre a un barrio
lanacion.description: La gestión de Jorge Macri inició una consulta vecinal ante “las inquietudes de la comunidad”

lanacion.title: Detuvieron a la expolicía que grababa contenido erótico tras protagonizar un choque fatal: le encontraron armas y drogas
lanacion.description: Se trata de Nicole Verón, quien fue expulsada de la fuerza en 2025 tras publicar videos sugestivos con su uniforme; fue tras un accidente vial en el que murió una persona; la liberaron horas después

lanacion.title: EE.UU. sanciona al presidente cubano Díaz-Canel y a miembros de la familia Castro
lanacion.description: La medida eleva la presión de la administración Trump al régimen comunista de la isla, que vive su peor crisis social desde el triunfo de la revolución

lanacion.title: España, un candidato del Mundial, sufre por Lamine Yamal y por su juego: apenas un tibio 1-1 con Irak
lanacion.description: Con algunas de sus figuras, no pudo contra un débil adversario en La Coruña

lanacion.description: El nuevo primer ministro húngaro revirtió la férrea negativa del gobierno ultranacionalista anterior, aliado del Kremlin, a permitir la adhesión de Ucrania al bloque de los 27

lanacion.title: Keiichi Toyoda, experto en filosofía samurái: “Una mente clara y concentrada permite adormecer el miedo”
lanacion.description: El escritor japonés, experto en entrenar la mente a través de los principios de las artes marciales, trabaja en la idea de explorar la filosofía samurái

phys-org.title: Deep-sea discovery uncovers new family of copepods near Greenland
phys-org.description: An international research team, including Dr. Nancy Mercado Salas from the Leibniz Institute for the Analysis of Biodiversity Change (LIB), has described a new family of copepods (Copepoda). The discovery was made at a depth of more than 2,500 meters in the Irminger Basin, southeast of Greenland, and provides new insights into the evolution of a group of animals that has hitherto been poorly understood. The findings are published in the journal PeerJ.

phys-org.title: School in a hot world: What research is saying about children's health and learning
phys-org.description: Climate change is making southern Africa hotter. While much attention has focused on climate impacts such as droughts, floods and food insecurity, another crisis is unfolding quietly inside classrooms. Research has shown that some schools are becoming dangerously hot places for children to develop, learn and play.

phys-org.title: Novel synthetic biomolecule degrades disease-related proteins
phys-org.description: Northwestern Medicine scientists have developed a novel synthetic biomolecular condensate that can degrade intracellular disease-causing proteins, providing a framework for new therapeutic approaches for a wide range of diseases, as detailed in a recent study published in Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Exploring the meanings of plants and hair, from Amazon pastures to suburban lawns and groomed bodies
phys-org.description: Cultivated lawns, cleared cattle pastures and carefully groomed hair all reflect a shared cultural logic, according to a new book by UC Santa Barbara anthropology professor Jeffrey Hoelle.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Why do telomeres shorten when a cell divides, and how does it affect human aging?
phys-org.description: In each cell of your body, DNA is stored in structures called chromosomes. When cells divide, these chromosomes are copied, but over time, the copying process degrades. After many cycles of making copies, the ends of the chromosomes become shorter and can sometimes get damaged. Thankfully, we have telomeres, which are like protective caps on the ends of our chromosomes that help to decrease the damage when cells divide.

phys-org.title: Record ultraviolet quasar wind reaches 30% light speed near supermassive black hole
phys-org.description: A team led by York University researchers has discovered the fastest wind near a supermassive black hole ever found at ultraviolet wavelengths, driven by the disk of matter (quasar) surrounding the black hole.

phys-org.title: New report finds sharply rising rates of unemployment for Black Californians
phys-org.description: Employment—a major marker and measure of quality of life—declined among Black Californians between 2024 and 2025, according to new research from the Black Policy Project, a research initiative of the UCLA Ralph J. Bunche Center for African American Studies.

phys-org.title: The best pollinators can drive evolutionary changes in flowers
phys-org.description: A new study by plant biologists at the University of California, Santa Cruz, challenges a longstanding idea that stems from the large number of flowers in the mountains of Central and South America that have evolved to be pollinated by hummingbirds instead of bees. According to the research team, flowers make this switch—not because bees avoid cool, wet cloud forest conditions at higher elevations—but because hummingbirds are simply more effective pollinators.

phys-org.title: Focus apps are failing neurodivergent minds, new research finds
phys-org.description: In today's attention economy, social media platforms, entertainment apps and news feeds all compete for our focus.

phys-org.title: Rare wild goats in Northumberland prove to be a genetically distinct breed
phys-org.description: New research shows Cheviot goats are one of the UK's most genetically distinct goat populations. Led by Newcastle University, this is the first genetic study to determine the ancestry and genetic health of a UK feral goat population. It provides a genetic assessment of the Cheviot goats in Northumberland's College Valley, identifying them as a historically significant and genetically distinct population unlike the other European goat breeds.

phys-org.title: Fossil fishes buried in the desert reveal a missing chapter in marine history
phys-org.description: When an asteroid struck Earth about 66 million years ago, it ended the age of dinosaurs and transformed life across the planet. The effects of that catastrophe are visible in the fossil record on land, but scientists know far less about what happened to fishes in the seas during the first few million years after the extinction.

phys-org.title: What makes 15-minute cities work? More nearby jobs and connected streets
phys-org.description: The concept of the "15-Minute City" has gained global traction as a blueprint for more livable, sustainable communities by placing daily essentials—such as grocery stores, schools, restaurants and parks—within easy reach of residents. The idea envisions neighborhoods where people can meet most of their daily needs within a 15-minute walk, bike ride or transit trip from home, reducing automobile dependence while improving quality of life.

phys-org.title: Bison restoration efforts and grazing rights hinge on one question: Are bison wildlife?
phys-org.description: Bison are political animals. A federal decision to revoke grazing leases for bison on public lands on the rolling plains of eastern Montana is the latest manifestation of long-standing contention. The largest land animal in North America, bison are considered a "keystone" species, meaning they have high ecological and cultural importance.

phys-org.title: Overlooked DNA structures help organize the genome
phys-org.description: Northwestern Medicine scientists have discovered that little-studied DNA structures play a central role in organizing the human genome and controlling gene activity, according to a new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The study revealed that G-quadruplexes (G4s)—four-stranded DNA structures—directly interact with a key genome-organizing protein called CTCF, helping shape how DNA folds inside the cell and how genes are turned on or off.

phys-org.title: Eroding a virtue: AI trains people to expect instant answers, and that's bad news for patience
phys-org.description: When I was growing up, teachers would assign research papers that required going to the library, or later, searching for relevant material on the internet. If the paper was going to turn out well, we students needed to patiently comb through piles of material, weaving what we found into a coherent argument that was well-supported with evidence.

phys-org.title: Atmosphere survival model refines search for habitable planets
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed the Smaller Than Earth Habitability Model (STEHM) to assess which planets can maintain life-supporting atmospheres, focusing on size and atmospheric dynamics.

phys-org.title: Teaching AI to design optical surfaces using real-world imperfections
phys-org.description: Designing surfaces that precisely control how light behaves at the nanoscale is tricky. Optical Fourier surfaces, which are nanostructured gratings that redistribute light into specific directions and wavelengths, hold enormous potential for compact spectrometers, augmented-reality displays, and advanced sensors. phys-org.title: Climate vulnerable residents in Nigeria are creating makeshift adaptation systems
phys-org.description: Residents in informal settlements in Lagos—who are among the most vulnerable to climate change—have developed sophisticated, multi-scale climate adaptation systems and are earning a living from climate action, a new study by Brianna Castro, assistant professor of urban sustainability at the Yale School of the Environment, found.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.

proj-syn.title: British Steel Needs a Transformation, Not a Bailout
proj-syn.description: The recent revival of industrial policy offers an opportunity to break the old pattern whereby economic risks are socialized while rewards remain privatized. In addition to attaching meaningful conditionalities to public support, governments must invest in the state capacity required to govern strategic sectors well.

proj-syn.title: How to Encourage Deceased Organ Donation
proj-syn.description: Developing countries facing organ shortages often search for complex solutions, such as sweeping legal reforms. But Tunisia’s experience suggests a much simpler first step: awareness-raising sessions where doctors explain how the transplant system works, and people share their fears and concerns.

proj-syn.title: Building Alliances of America’s Allies
proj-syn.description: In a world in which the US cannot be counted on as it once was, the objective is not stability at any price, but rather stability on terms consistent with national and Western interests. This is achievable, but only if the friends of the US recognize the new reality and act individually and collectively to meet the challenge.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Limits of African Data Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: African countries are recognizing that no matter how well-designed their data-protection regulations are, their sovereignty over US-based Big Tech firms ends at the boundary between subsidiary and parent. Overcoming this barrier will require a level of coordination that the continent has yet to achieve.

proj-syn.title: The AI Economy’s Permanent Underclass
proj-syn.description: AI is transforming the global economy while widening the gap between technological winners and losers. Governments that fail to secure a place in the AI supply chain may find themselves confronting mass job displacement without the tax revenues or state capacity needed to contain the social and political fallout.

proj-syn.title: The Rape of Venezuela
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s oil production is rising, yet its currency is depreciating, inflation is accelerating, and foreign exchange remains scarce. The disconnect reflects a political economy built on private dealmaking and a mutually beneficial alliance between ruling elites and US President Donald Trump’s acolytes.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

crunchbase.description: Overall, May’s active investor tallies painted a picture of a startup funding scene still dominated by familiar names.

crunchbase.description: All-in-one software ecosystem provider Scotch is a Denver-based AI-native operating system designed specifically for liquor store owners.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Funding Pushed Startup Investment To Near-Record Levels In May As Exit Market Reopened
crunchbase.description: All told, global venture funding reached $92 billion in May, marking the second-largest monthly total on record, just behind February, Crunchbase data shows. Of that, Anthropic raised $50 billion, or 54% of the month’s total funding.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Defense Startup Funding Hits An All-Time Record As VCs Begin To Eye Exits
crunchbase.description: Already this year, more than $14.6 billion in venture investment has gone into companies in Crunchbase’s military, national security and law enforcement categories, blowing past the sector's previous annual record of $9.6 billion raised in all of 2025.

crunchbase.title: SaaS Is Dead. Long Live SaaS! AI And The End Of The Rationing Of Knowledge Work
crunchbase.description: Reports of “SaaS being dead” are misguided, writes guest author Bob Morse, who contends that AI will enable software companies to move beyond selling productivity tools to deliver knowledge-work outcomes directly, unlocking massive unmet demand for services, ultimately growing the software industry.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Files Confidentially For IPO
crunchbase.description: Anthropic said Monday that it has submitted a confidential filing for a proposed IPO, marking an escalation in the race among generative AI behemoths to make it first to the public market.

crunchbase.title: How I Raised $14M For My Startup When I Stopped Pitching And Started Speaking
crunchbase.description: When investor trust is built through repeated in-person encounters, authentic conversations and thought leadership on meaningful problems, relationships and visibility matter more than aggressive fundraising outreach, argues guest author Alyx van der Vorm, whose startup raised $14 million as the result of personal interactions.

crunchbase.title: Boston Startup Fundraising Looks Strong Only By Pre-AI Parameters
crunchbase.description: So far this year, investors have put about $7.8 billion into Boston-area startups, per Crunchbase data. That puts the region on track for a moderate annual gain and the strongest tally in about four years.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Anthropic Dominates In An Otherwise Slower Week For Megarounds
crunchbase.description: Venture funding has always been a world of haves and have nots. And these days, the haves are having more than ever. Case in point this week was generative AI giant Anthropic's $65 billion Series H funding, followed by a billion-dollar funding for an AI software developer.

crunchbase.title: They Saw Women Shut Out Of VC, So A PayPal Veteran And Former Navy Officer Built An Alternative
crunchbase.description: Co-founded by Molly Huyck and Amie Konwinski, Aequitas Invest's funding portal provides women-led businesses a way to raise capital. Crunchbase News recently spoke to the founders to learn more about their plans to help female entrepreneurs raise and hold on to more equity.
